title: Type-scale sprawl and a legibility floor problem
description:
web/src/index.css uses ~28 distinct font sizes (the review says "30+"); the most common are
0.78rem (~12.5px) and 0.72rem (~11.5px), with sizes down to 0.62rem (~10px). Most of the
app's information — macro chips, legends, captions, microcopy — lives below 13px, much of
it in `--muted` gray.

Contrast: on the light theme `--muted` (#64748b) on `--bg` (#e8ecf3) is right at the AA
boundary, and the olive accent (#859900) on white measures ~3.2:1 — below the 4.5:1
required for normal-size text, which matters because kcal values on every food card use it.

Direction: adopt a small tokenized scale (12 / 13 / 15 / 17 / 20 / 24) and migrate by
find-and-replace tiers rather than redesign. Floor: nothing informational below 12px.
Keep inputs >=16px to avoid iOS auto-zoom.

Sequenced third in the review "before new screens multiply the size count further".
Worth doing as one token pass with ct-m10.1.
acceptance_criteria: A tokenized type scale replaces ad-hoc sizes; nothing informational renders below 12px; inputs are >=16px; accent-on-surface and muted-on-bg pairs pass 4.5:1 in every theme.

title: M10 — IA pass: unified nutrition/fullness + FF transparency
description:
Two complaints: nutrition/fullness is presented with different grammars in different
places (per-entry pill, per-meal pill, day meter, bare numbers in editors, and now M8's
`guideScore` vocabulary), and it is unclear how the Fullness Factor is calculated / hard
to score high.

**Decided:** do not change the FF formula. The absolute number being hard to max is
correct — FF measures a fixed property of a food. Re-anchoring the tiers would make
"moderate" feel better without being more truthful. The real issue is that FF is the
wrong *headline* for most decisions, so fix the framing with one headline per context.

10.2 and 10.3 shipped (verified at HEAD). 10.1 and 10.4 remain.

title: Balance gauge is direction-blind and red every afternoon
description:
Two defects: the dial compared the *running* balance against an *end-of-day* plan balance,
so it was deep red every afternoon by construction and could only turn green near bedtime;
and red-at-both-ends reads simply as "bad" on a tinted ring, so a month of
losing-faster-than-goal rendered identically to a month of overeating.
close_reason: Shipped (working tree, not yet committed): the dial now judges projectedBalanceKcal, shows a shaded +/-150 kcal on-plan zone, and balanceColor() is direction-aware (green->red above plan, green->blue for a steeper-than-goal deficit). Trends bars share the ramp; the Cumulative line switched to a neutral stroke

title: Trends still plots today's bar from the running so-far balance
description:

title: Log plan summary is alarm-fatigued prose
description: Two center-aligned sentences of math repeated each other, one with red inline text and one entirely orange — the noisiest element on the app's most-visited screen, screaming on what is arguably good news.
close_reason: Shipped (working tree, not yet committed): one status line plus one action line in a neutral color. The recommended intake is now quoted as its stable base (BMR + baseline + goal balance) "plus what you burn", fixing the old total that lowballed mornings and drifted up as workouts landed

title: Log hero asks the user to reconcile five numbers and three palettes
description:
Consumed (+1643, macro-colored ring), Burned (-3151, expenditure-colored ring), Balance
(-1507, red ring with "1122 below plan" nested inside), plus the deficit math below. Three
adjacent donuts each use a different color system with no legend on screen. The signed
numbers duplicate what the labels say, and the signs flip meaning between rings.

Direction: pick one hero number — "remaining to eat today" is the classic for good reason —
and render it large in a single ring. Demote Consumed/Burned to a compact row; put the
macro and expenditure breakdowns one tap away. Drop the +/- signs.

The review flags this as "the only item here that needs real product thought; worth a quick
mock before code." Overlaps ct-m10.4.

Note: ct-m14.4's Simple dashboard already does roughly this for Simple view — the open
question is Detailed.

title: Trends has three overlapping navigation systems
description:
Chevrons, zoom steppers, seven range presets, *and* a mini-map scrubber — eleven controls wrapping onto two rows before any chart appears. The scrubber's handles also render clipped at the right edge.

Direction: keep the presets and the scrubber (or presets + drag/pinch on the chart itself, since `TrendGestureSurface` exists); drop the chevron and zoom chips. One row of controls, more chart above the fold.

title: Series color collision on Calories by macro
description:
Carbs bars (#d97706) and the Burned line (orange family, introduced by ct-m7.3) are near-neighbors, adjacent in the legend, and overlapping in the plot. The dashed "intake target" label also collides with the trend-line label area.

Direction: move Burned to a hue no macro uses (the teal `--exp-baseline` family, or a neutral) and nudge labels apart. A five-series legend under a dense chart is at the limit — consider making Burned and Trend toggleable.

title: Header real estate and a permanently promoted Sign out
description:
Every screen spends its top bar on the static app name plus a permanent Sign out button — the most dangerous common action, promoted app-wide. Meanwhile page identity lives only in the tab bar.

Direction: contextual header title (page name or date); move Sign out into the existing SettingsMenu behind the gear.

title: Quick-add microcopy is insider shorthand
description:
"0.9x 1 bowl (recycle) 576x" packs multiplier, unit, and log-count into a string only its author can read confidently. The check-in-circle quick-add works, but olive kcal text next to a green check button gives two competing "go" signals per card.

Direction: spell the count ("logged 576x" in the muted row) or drop it — its main job is ranking, which the sort order already expresses. Keep kcal in `--text` weight so the check button is the only action-colored element.

title: Reframe FF per context rather than recalibrating tiers
description:
The `41.7*cal^-0.7` term dominates, so FF is essentially inverse calorie density: a
25-50 kcal/100g vegetable hits 4-5 while a normal composite plate lands ~1.8-2.3 almost
regardless of protein.

Decision: keep the formula, change the headline per context — per individual food, show FF
relative to the user's own logged foods ("more filling than ~80% of what you eat"); per
meal / menu choice / Guide, make the goal-aware `choiceScore` the headline with FF as one
labeled input inside its breakdown.

Verified at HEAD: `fullnessPercentile()` at web/src/lib/fullness.ts:116, called from
FullnessBadge.tsx:47; `choiceScore` promoted into web/src/lib/choiceScan.ts and shared.
close_reason: fullnessPercentile() + shared choiceScore shipped; formula deliberately unchanged (commit d7c6f97, 2026-06-17)

title: Log-page IA sweep
description:
With Guide/Menu (M8) and theming (M9) added, make one explicit pass over the tab shell
(Log / Trends / Goals — where do Guide / Menu / Chat live?) and the EnergySummary stack
ordering. Scoped to one deliberate pass, not a wholesale redo.

Overlaps ct-dr.4 (the Log hero asks the user to reconcile five numbers and three
palettes), which is the most concrete instance of this problem.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md 10.4.

title: M11 — Meal photos & visual identity
description:
Capture photos are already persisted (/data/photos, served at /photos/<ref>) and entries
carry `photo_ref`, but the photo is never resurfaced — entry rows were text-only.

Research summary: MyFitnessPal / Lose It! put a thumbnail on the diary row plus a separate
photo timeline; Foodvisor / Bitesnap make the photo *be* the log; Cronometer leans on
food-group icons only; Yazio / Lifesum use friendly category illustrations when there is
no photo. Takeaway: two complementary directions — real thumbnails where we have them, and
category icons so every row still gets a visual identity.

11.3 (icons) shipped. Thumbnails and the gallery remain.

Note: the doc rollup table marks this milestone "not started" even though 11.3 shipped —
one of the status contradictions that motivated moving to a tracker.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 11".

title: Thumbnails on entry rows
description:
Show a small `photo_ref` thumbnail on EntryRow when present; tap -> full image in a Modal.
Needs a resized variant (a `?w=96` handled by the static layer, or a thumbnail generated
on upload in app/storage.py) so the diary does not pull full-res photos.

Per-item split (M6) shares one photo across rows — decide: show it on each, or only the
first.

Verified absent at HEAD: no `photo_ref` reference in web/src/components/EntryRow.tsx.
Depends on ct-cr.11 in spirit — /photos is currently unauthenticated, so making photos
first-class raises the priority of fixing that.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md 11.1.
acceptance_criteria: Thumbnails load a resized variant (verify payload size), not full-res; tapping opens the full image.

title: Category icons / visual-form fallback
description:
Every entry row leads with a theme-tinted chip showing the food's **visual form** (its
vessel/silhouette), not a nutritional category. Two decoupled layers: a resolver
(food -> category key, web/src/lib/foodCategory.ts) and a renderer (key -> SVG,
web/src/lib/foodCategoryIcons.tsx + FoodIcon), so the icon style can be re-skinned without
touching the mapping. Taxonomy is 2-tier (~20 form-based Tier-1 groups + ~100 Tier-2),
mirrored in app/categories.py.

Classification: the AI emits a Tier-1 `category`; barcodes derive a Tier-2 from Open Food
Facts `categories_tags`; a nullable `category` column persists it. Guardrails: a barcode
Tier-2 wins outright; else the trusted AI group polices the keyword Tier-2 guess;
word-boundary matching avoids substring traps; nothing confident -> a neutral generic.

Design north star: group by what a food *looks like on the table*, because that is what an
icon can honestly represent — which is why `breakfast` (a time) and a single `beverages`
bucket are dissolved by vessel.

Tests: web/src/lib/foodCategory.test.ts, tests/test_categories.py. The audit script
web/scripts/auditCategories.ts over the seeded personas shows 0 generic.
Follow-up commit 5ee1bd4 swapped in Fluent Emoji Flat SVG icons.
close_reason: Wave A shipped: resolver + renderer + 2-tier taxonomy + guardrails, 0 generic in the persona audit (commit 7234d5a, 2026-06-21)

title: M12 — Conversational meal & restaurant assistant / recipes
description:
The generative layer on top of M8's menu scanner.

**Decided:** start structured, not freeform chat — a few canned questions plus a free-text
box, single-shot. Cheaper, easier to keep grounded in the real menu/macros, and it can
grow into multi-turn later. Gate every call behind an explicit button, never automatic.
Lives on the Guide page or the menu-scan result screen, not a new top-level tab unless it
earns one (ties into ct-m10.4).

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 12".

title: Recipes / make it at home
description:
From a logged meal or a craving, generate a recipe scaled to a target ("a 600 kcal,
45 g-protein version of this burrito bowl") -> ingredients + steps + an estimated macro
breakdown that one-taps into the existing entry-create path (reuse the estimate schema +
EstimateCard / batch).

Also P1 #8 in docs/PRODUCT_OPPORTUNITIES.md ("Recipe builder and batch leftovers").

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md 12.2.
acceptance_criteria: A generated recipe's macros round-trip into an entry via the existing batch path.

title: Cost: capture & surface
description:
An optional `price`/`cost` on entries (reuse the menu `price`). Surface cost-per-meal and
cost-per-day, and — with macros — cost per 100 kcal and cost per gram of protein (the
"protein on a budget" view people actually want). Mostly a nullable column + migration
following the `_migrate_add_columns` pattern, an editor input, and a couple of derived
readouts.

Verified absent at HEAD: no price/cost field on app/models.py.
Also P2 #7 in docs/PRODUCT_OPPORTUNITIES.md.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md 13.1.
acceptance_criteria: Migration test for the new column (tests/test_migration.py pattern); cost per g protein computes correctly.

title: Cost in ranking + a value sort
description: Add cost as an optional term to the Guide/Menu `choiceScore`: when prices are present, prefer cheaper at equal nutrition; expose a "value" sort (best nutrition per dollar). Extends existing scoring, no new infra.

title: Taste rating (would eat again)
description:
Let the user rate logged foods 1-5, stored per food (or per `SavedFood` once ct-m1.4.2
lands — hence the dependency). Use it to (a) re-rank Guide suggestions toward foods you
actually like and (b) flag "healthy but you rated low" so suggestions are not joyless —
the antidote to a guide that only optimizes nutrition. Frecency is a weak implicit taste
signal that could seed it.

Verified absent at HEAD. Also P2 #6 in docs/PRODUCT_OPPORTUNITIES.md.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md 13.3.
acceptance_criteria: Taste rating persists per user and demonstrably shifts Guide order; never aggregated or shared across users.

title: M14 — Simple/Detailed view + meal-first logging
description:
Driven by first-time-user feedback: the Log page reads as too cluttered, picking a meal
*after* starting to log feels backwards, macros are not wanted, and "Balance" is not
understood. Diagnosis: the friction is real, but the fix is better defaults and
disclosure, not stripping features.

Decided: one unified toggle (not two); no new per-meal routes; keep the EstimateCard meal
selector as a pre-filled correction affordance.

All five sub-items verified shipped at HEAD. NOTE: docs/BACKLOG.md still marks this
milestone and its rollup row as partial — the doc is stale.
close_reason: All five sub-items shipped and verified in code; backlog doc status was stale (commit 1de1a4c, 2026-06-20)

title: Simple/Detailed view toggle
description:
One persisted per-page switch. In Simple view, per-meal/per-entry macros and the
staying-power adornment collapse, and the energy summary drops the Consumed/Burned/Balance
rings. One control answers "too cluttered" + "don't care about macros" + "don't understand
Balance" at once.

Verified at HEAD: `DEFAULT_SIMPLE_VIEW` in web/src/lib/viewMode.ts, consumed by
web/src/lib/ThemeProvider.tsx. The default later flipped to Simple for new users
(recorded in docs/DESIGN_REVIEW.md's July 12 status); Detailed is the opt-in enthusiast
view. Possible fast-follow from the doc: split into two toggles if power users want macros
while simplifying Balance.
close_reason: Persisted toggle shipped; default later flipped to Simple for new users (commit 4e03594, 2026-06-19)

title: Meal-first logging
description:
All four meals render always (even empty), each with an "+ Add to {meal}" button that scopes the capture flow to that meal up front (LogPage -> `CapturePage initialMeal`), so the meal is chosen before logging instead of via a mid-flow dropdown. The global Food button stays as a time-defaulted quick path.

Verified at HEAD: `initialMeal` in web/src/pages/CapturePage.tsx, passed from web/src/pages/LogPage.tsx.

title: Grouped entry surface
description:
A section's entries read as one bordered card with inset dividers (`.entry-list--grouped`) instead of one floating card per row — applied to both meals and exercise. Entry names wrap up to 3 lines, then truncate.

Verified at HEAD: `.entry-list--grouped` in web/src/components/ExerciseSection.tsx and web/src/index.css.

title: MyNetDiary-style Simple dashboard
description:
The Simple energy view is a big "kcal left" ring over a grid of at-a-glance tiles — Breakfast/Lunch/Dinner/Snacks (kcal) + Exercise + Steps. Meal tiles are tappable shortcuts into that meal's capture flow, reusing 14.2's wiring. No Water tile — the app does not track water.

Verified at HEAD: `SimpleEnergySummary` in web/src/components/EnergySummary.tsx.

title: Explicit Budget calorie framing
description:
The ring's net math (`goal + exercise - eaten`) was confusing because exercise silently
inflated the goal. Now an explicit `Budget = goal + exercise` caption sits above the ring,
the big number is `left` (`budget - eaten`), the ring fills relative to the budget, and the
composition is spelled out below.

Caveat (conditional, already mitigated): `calorie_target` is a stored user-set field
(default flat 2,000), so it normally carries no activity allowance and the budget is
correct. Double-counting only arises if a user both applies the TDEE recommendation and
keeps a non-sedentary activity factor — which GoalsPage already warns against.
See ct-m14.6.

title: M2 — Multi-user via Google OAuth + email allowlist
description:
`User` model + app/auth.py (Google ID-token verify + session JWT) + auth router
(`/auth/google`, `/auth/me`, `/auth/logout`); real `get_current_user` + the shared
`user_query` scoping helper in app/deps.py; every data route scoped by `user_id`;
owner-email backfill of pre-auth rows. Frontend login gate + Google Identity Services
button, `credentials: 'include'`, build-time `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` threaded through
the Dockerfile.

Foundational — M3, M4, and M5 all build on the per-user scoping.
Note: closed access by design. Public signup is tracked separately as ct-cr.8.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 2".
close_reason: Google ID-token verify + session JWT + per-user scoping across every route (commit 4adcd52, 2026-06-01)

title: M3 — Health metrics & insights
description:
Weight/body-fat logging with goals, a Recharts trends view, and a TDEE/BMR target recommender.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 3".
close_reason: 3.1 + 3.2 + 3.3 all shipped, plus three items beyond the original plan (commit f1e3165, 2026-06-01)

title: Weight & body-fat logging + body goals
description: `BodyMetric` model (one row/user/day) + `/api/metrics` (POST upsert / GET-range / DELETE); `goal_weight_kg` / `goal_body_fat_pct` / `weekly_rate_kg` on `Targets`; canonical kg with a kg/lb toggle (web/src/lib/units.ts); body-goals UI on GoalsPage.

title: Progress / Trends view (Recharts)
description: `GET /api/entries/range` (reuses day-summary aggregation); lazy-loaded TrendsPage with a stacked calories-by-macro bar + 7-day moving average + target reference line; weight and body-fat lines with an EMA-smoothed trend (web/src/lib/stats.ts); a 7/30/90-day range selector.

title: TDEE/BMR + adaptive target recommender
description: `height_cm`, `birth_year`, `sex`, `activity_factor` on the profile/`Targets`; Mifflin-St Jeor BMR x activity = TDEE in web/src/lib/tdee.ts; GoalsPage recommends a calorie target for the chosen `weekly_rate_kg`, and the adaptive variant infers real TDEE from the trailing 28-day weight trend vs intake.

title: Editable entry dates (backfill a forgotten meal)
description: Date picker in the create (EstimateCard) and edit (EntryRow) flows; helpers `dayKeyOf` / `withDayKey` in web/src/lib/date.ts.

title: Weight / body-fat backfill via a date picker
description: Date picker on the Trends quick-log card. (That card was later removed by ct-m4.1 — backfilling now happens by navigating to the day on Log.)

title: Body metric on the Log page
description: MetricCard shows a day's weight/body-fat like an entry row with the same edit/delete buttons, only on days that have one.

title: M4 — Information architecture & navigation
description:
Inspired by Cronometer's per-day action bar: add anything to the day you are *viewing*,
not a separate "today"-only tab. Adopted the idea, kept a simpler surface (food,
biometric, exercise — no notes/fasting).

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 4".
close_reason: 4.1 + 4.2 shipped; the capture tab is gone and Trends is view-only (commit 2e9b35b, 2026-06-17)

title: Fold Add into the Log page; act on the viewed day
description:
The `capture` tab is gone — App.tsx tabs are Log / Trends / Goals. LogPage has an action
bar (Food / Exercise / Weight) that opens the relevant editor in a Modal bound to the
viewed day: Food -> CapturePage, Exercise -> AddExercise, Weight -> the extracted
MetricEditor (shared by add + edit). The Trends weight quick-log card was removed.

Exercise on the day exceeded the original plan, which listed only Food + Biometric.
close_reason: Capture tab removed; day-bound action bar + shared MetricEditor shipped (commit 2e9b35b, 2026-06-17)

title: Navigation: calendar day-picker + click-a-Trends-value -> open that day
description:
A DayPicker month-grid popover opens from `.day-nav__label` and marks days with data;
clicking a Trends bar/point calls `goToDay(dayKey)`, which was lifted to App.tsx (sets
`tab='log'` + the day) and threaded into TrendsPage.

React Router was not adopted — deep links and browser-back remain optional. See ct-rf.2.
close_reason: DayPicker + goToDay lifted to App.tsx; cross-tab day navigation works (commit 2e9b35b, 2026-06-17)

title: Unify the capture composer (search + AI description + photo)
description:
The Food modal now uses one composer input for both recent-food search and new AI
descriptions. Picking a photo creates a preview first; the same input becomes optional
photo context before an explicit Estimate action, and recent-food matches hide while a
photo is attached. Barcode scanning remains a separate package-focused action.

Landed across three commits: 0c1b90d (unify composer + fuzzy search, 2026-06-21),
83d9c7c (boot splash + streamline, 2026-06-24), 4fce884 (stabilize search UX, 2026-06-27).
Recorded in the backlog as a "Capture composer update" note under 4.1.
close_reason: Unified composer + fuzzy recent-food search, stabilized over 0c1b90d -> 83d9c7c -> 4fce884 (commit 4fce884, 2026-06-27)

title: M5 — Activity & burned
description:
Shipped with a different model than the original sketch: no single `Burned` row —
steps live on `BodyMetric` and workouts are their own `ExerciseEntry` table, which made
per-workout edit/delete and the M7 range endpoint natural.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 5".
close_reason: ExerciseEntry + steps on BodyMetric + free-text AI estimate + net/gross toggle (commit f1e3165, 2026-06-01)

title: ExerciseEntry model + CRUD; steps on BodyMetric
description: `ExerciseEntry` (`user_id`, `date`, `name`, `calories`, ...) with CRUD in app/routers/exercise.py; `steps` added to `BodyMetric`. Tests: tests/test_exercise.py.

title: Steps -> calories
description: `stepsToKcal` (web/src/lib/activity.ts) using the latest weigh-in weight; step count entered on the metric/weight editor.

title: Exercise logging UI + free-text AI estimate
description: An Exercise action on the Log page -> AddExercise (manual kcal + name) and a per-day ExerciseSection. Free-text AI estimate: `analyze_activity_text` + `POST /api/analyze/activity` (MET-table system prompt -> kcal + name). Double-count guard left to the user as planned. Tests: tests/test_analyze_activity.py.

title: Net-calorie integration + persistent net/gross toggle
description: EnergySummary has a persistent net/gross toggle built on `burnedBreakdown` (BMR + activity + exercise + step burn); per-day burned is threaded through LogPage.

title: Per-item nutrition in the analysis schema + prompts
description: Extended each `items[]` element (and the strict `FOOD_ANALYSIS_JSON_SCHEMA`) with per-item `weight_g`, `fiber_g`, `sugar_g`, `sodium_mg`, `is_beverage`. Both prompts updated to estimate these per item and to define the dish/drink item boundary with a worked example. A real per-item `weight_g` is what makes the split trustworthy — it avoids a proportional-by-calories hack.

title: Batch create endpoint POST /api/entries/batch
description: Takes `{entries: EntryCreate[]}`, inserts in one transaction, returns `EntryRead[]` — atomic, one round-trip, one cache invalidation. User-scoped exactly like `create_entry`. Tests in tests/test_entries.py.

title: Review card -> per-item rows with a Combine action
description: `draftFromAnalysis` returns a list of item-drafts; EstimateCard became a multi-row editor (per-row macro editor + FullnessBadge + Drink toggle + select checkbox) with shared meal/date/photo. Combine merges selected rows (`is_beverage` true only if every merged item is a drink). Single-item captures and recent re-logs stay one row — no forced list chrome.

title: M7 — Trends: burned line + energy-balance weight prediction
description:
Activity/burned had shipped but never made it onto the Trends charts — it was only shown
for "today" in EnergySummary. This surfaced burned across the range and used the daily
intake - burned balance to predict weight change, so the modeled trajectory can be read
against the actual scale.

All math reuses existing helpers — no new formulas: `burnedBreakdown`, `stepsToKcal`,
`KCAL_PER_KG` (7700).

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 7".
close_reason: 7.1-7.5 shipped plus three items beyond the original plan (forecast chart, goal-progress tracks, body composition) (commit 6e55e10, 2026-06-19)

title: Per-day exercise totals endpoint GET /api/exercise/range
description: Mirrors `entries_range`: group `ExerciseEntry` by `date`, sum `calories`, return a sparse `list[ExerciseDaySummary]`. Client `getExerciseRange(from, to)`.

title: Shared per-day burned series memo
description: An `exercise-range` query plus a shared `burnedByDay` memo consumed by 7.3/7.4/7.5. Weight is forward-filled per day (BMR needs a weight daily but weigh-ins are sparse); returns null on an incomplete profile so burned features hide and charts degrade to prior behavior.

title: Burned line on the calories chart
description: The gap between the stacked-bar top (consumed) and the line is the day's deficit/surplus at a glance. Gated on profile completeness. (The chosen orange collides with the carbs bar — see ct-dr.6.)

title: Energy-balance chart with sign-colored net bars
description: `net = consumed - burned` per day as bars colored by sign, a zero ReferenceLine, and a cumulative-net line. Header readout: total net kcal over the range and an approximate kg via `KCAL_PER_KG`.

title: Predicted-weight line vs actual
description:
Walks the axis accumulating `dailyNet` only on days with logged intake — never treating an
unlogged day as a giant deficit.

**Superseded during implementation:** the anchor now sits at the *most recent* smoothed
weigh-in and projects forward only (not the first weight in range), via
`predictWeightSeries` (web/src/lib/forecast.ts) + `emaByDate`, so the line re-anchors to
recent scale readings across travel gaps.
close_reason: Shipped, then re-anchored to the latest weigh-in with a forward-only projection (commit 4c3c0f8, 2026-06-17)

title: Weight-forecast chart with an uncertainty cone
description: A dedicated card extending the axis past->future to the goal-pace finish date: actuals + EMA trend, the Goal-pace projection, and a Predicted line extrapolated at the recent average daily balance, with both ETAs read out. Shades a heuristic uncertainty band (`bandHalfWidthKg`) — see ct-bl.7 for making it data-driven.

title: Goal-progress tracks per metric
description: GoalProgress: per-metric (weight / body fat) progress bars on the metric's own scale with a predicted-pace marker, range-independent.

title: Body composition chart + coherent body-fat forecast
description:
web/src/lib/composition.ts derives lean and fat mass from `weight x (1 - bf/100)`. A Body
composition card stacks fat + lean over the measured range plus a lean-held-steady
forecast. The weight chart's body-fat projection is no longer an independent glide to the
BF goal — it is derived from the predicted-weight line (`predictBodyFatSeries`, lean held
constant), so weight change and body-fat change stay consistent.

Tested in web/src/lib/composition.test.ts. Possible follow-ups noted in the doc:
a data-driven lean-trend partition instead of holding lean constant; an optional
lean-mass goal.

title: M8 — Food Guide + Menu scanner
description:
Carries the data hooks later milestones need: a goal-aware `choiceScore` (feeds M10) and
a per-item `price` (feeds M13).

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 8".
close_reason: Guide page + menu scanner shipped with tests (commit 5859832, 2026-06-14)

title: Guide page: rank your own logged foods for your goal
description: GuidePage + web/src/lib/guide.ts rank logged/recent foods for lose/gain/maintain via `rankGuideFoods` -> `rankFoodChoices` (web/src/lib/choiceScan.ts): a `choiceScore` blending fullness, protein-per-100kcal, fiber-per-100kcal, a calorie penalty, and beverage / low-fullness penalties. Plus curated static idea lists. Tests: web/src/lib/guide.test.ts, choiceScan.test.ts.

title: Menu scanner: photograph a menu -> ranked best choices
description: MenuScanner / ChoiceScanResults / MenuPhotoPreview -> `POST /api/analyze/menu` extracts `MenuOption[]` (name, description, section, price, serving estimate, macros, `is_beverage`, confidence) -> `choicesFromMenuResult` -> a ranked list sortable by recommended / menu / calories / protein / fullness. Tests: tests/test_analyze_menu.py.

title: M9 — UI theming (5 themes) + Settings menu
description:
Decided to ship all five themes at once rather than Light/Dark first: the plumbing
(tokens + chart map + settings + picker) is the real cost and is paid once, and building
the token contract against five palettes up front avoids baking in dark-only assumptions.

Themes: Light, Dark (slate), Black (GitHub), Cool (Solarized), Warm (Gruvbox), plus System
— which resolves to a user-chosen dark variant at night.

**Follow-up owed to M10:** the palettes were authored against the *current* token set.
When ct-m10.1 adds fiber/satiety hues, those tokens must be added to all five
`[data-theme]` blocks and all five chart palettes.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 9".
close_reason: All five themes + System + Settings sheet + no-flash bootstrap shipped (commit 4f6eeb1, 2026-06-14)

title: Token architecture: per-theme [data-theme] blocks
description: `:root` is the dark base; each theme overrides tokens via `:root[data-theme='...']`. Every hard-coded color routed through tokens (tints via `color-mix()`; new `--bg-deep / --on-accent / --overlay / --shadow / --reticle` + a `--fullness-*` 5-tier ramp). Only the camera letterbox stays intentionally black.

title: Chart palette per theme
description: Recharts writes fill/stroke as SVG presentation attributes that cannot read `var()`, so a theme has two surfaces to drive. Solved with a palette-per-theme in web/src/lib/colors.ts consumed through `useChartColors()`.

title: Settings sheet as the home for prefs
description: SettingsMenu opens from a header gear, with swatch previews. Intended as the home for prefs currently scattered or implicit (kg/lb, net/gross default, future ones). See ct-dr.7 — Sign out should move in here too.

title: Theme picker + persistence with no flash
description: `usePersistentChoice` added next to `usePersistentToggle`; a System option; an inline bootstrap in web/index.html applies the saved theme + iOS `theme-color` before first paint.

title: All five palettes
description: Light; Dark (slate); GitHub dark; Solarized dark; Gruvbox dark — macro/burned/fullness hues mapped into each palette's spirit, not just the neutrals, and mirrored in the JS chart map. Light was the most per-palette work (shadows/overlays tuned for dark needed light counterparts).

title: Refactor checkpoints
description:
Architectural cleanups tracked alongside feature milestones.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Refactor checkpoints".
close_reason: All five checkpoints done; React Router remains deliberately un-adopted (commit 4c3c0f8, 2026-06-17)

title: Real current_user dependency + single user_query scoping helper
description: Landed in app/deps.py; no router hand-writes the user_id filter.

title: Lift goToDay(dayKey) to App.tsx
description: Sets `tab` + day, so cross-tab "go to day" works from Trends. React Router still not adopted — deep links and browser-back remain optional, deliberately.

title: Opportunistic cleanups
description: GoalsPage setState-in-effect fixed (query-wrapper + form-from-props); the 3.2 range endpoint reuses day-summary aggregation; unused `DailyTotals`/`EntryList` components deleted.

title: Extract the useNumericDraft hook
description: Transient empty/partial field while focused, commit-on-valid, re-sync on blur — shared by MacroInput, ServingsStepper, and NumberField.

title: Extract CHART_COLORS mapped by concept
description: Recharts SVG attrs cannot read CSS `var()`, so the palette lives in web/src/lib/colors.ts mapped by concept. Later made theme-aware by ct-m9.2.

title: Body card delete affordance is unlabeled
description: The bare x that deletes a body log sits unlabeled next to the attachment icon at the top of the Log. Give destructive actions distance or a confirm.

title: Guide page affordances don't signal readable vs pressable
description: The "Find servings with staying power" card looks tappable but has no CTA or chevron; the "LOSS" eyebrow is blunt to the point of ambiguity ("FOR WEIGHT LOSS" reads better). The page mixes an explainer, a tool, and a ranked list — each card should signal whether it is readable or pressable.

title: Trends expand icon overlaps the tab bar
description: The expand icon overlaps the tab bar / "Goals" label at the bottom of the screenshot — check z-index and safe-area placement.

title: Staying power legend is stated twice on the Log
description: Right-aligned text and the chip legend below the bar say the same thing. Once is enough.

title: Composer modal can only be dismissed from the top-right x
description: On a phone that is the hardest corner to reach. Swipe-down-to-dismiss or a bottom-anchored cancel would match the sheet metaphor.

title: Emoji in functional chrome
description: Full-color emoji work beautifully for food identity but muddy functional controls — the color camera emoji inside the olive "Add photo" button and the four tab-bar emoji at different visual weights read slightly off. Consider monochrome glyphs for chrome, emoji for content.

title: Product maturity / showcase priorities
description:
Seven priorities framed around portfolio/showcase value rather than user value. These are
themes, not tickets — each carries a "Definition of done" (captured as acceptance criteria)
and a "Proof point target" résumé line in the source doc.

Explicitly argued as LOW showcase-ROI in this doc: broad wellness features (water, fasting,
habits, streaks), and cosmetic-only polish.

Source: docs/PRODUCT_MATURITY_ROADMAP.md.

title: Support / admin scripts

title: Product opportunities & differentiators
description:
Positioning and differentiator bets. Children are only the candidate-backlog items that
are NOT already tracked elsewhere — saved foods/meals, onboarding, LLM quota, authenticated
photos, the restaurant assistant, recipes, water, taste, and cost all have canonical beads
under M1/M12/M13/CR and are not duplicated here.

**Avoid For Now** (from the doc, recorded so it is not re-litigated): a giant public food
database built from scratch; a full social network; a huge recipe catalog; a meal-plan
marketplace; a generic open-ended health chatbot; punitive gamification; heavy badge
economies, leaderboards, or loot-box rewards; and any feature that adds AI calls
automatically without user intent.

description: The Trends weight forecast currently shades a heuristic uncertainty band (`bandHalfWidthKg`: daily-noise floor + a linear systematic-bias term, capped). title: Smarter normalization / dedup of recent foods
description:
Dedup is exact case-insensitive trimmed name, so "Greek yogurt", "greek yogurt bowl",
and "Greek Yogurt (1 cup)" fragment into separate chips. Normalize more before grouping
(trailing parentheticals, serving suffixes, punctuation) — conservatively, to avoid
merging genuinely different foods. Pairs with 1.4r.b's GROUP BY key.

title: M13 — Cost & taste as optimization dimensions
description:
Today the app optimizes purely on nutrition. Cost and taste add two more axes: quality
food can be expensive, and some healthy food is less tasty.

The menu scanner already extracts a per-option `price`, so cost data is already flowing
for restaurant menus — just unused in scoring.

**Decided:** cheapest, tastiest, and most nutritious rarely coincide — do not fold them
into one opaque number. Expose separate sortable dimensions (nutrition / value / foods you
like) so the user picks the trade-off, consistent with M10's "don't hide it in one score"
stance. Taste is per-user and subjective — never aggregate or share it. Manual cost entry
is the realistic v1; per-region grocery-price APIs are out of scope.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 13".

title: Make the double-count hint conditional

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md 14.5 "Possible follow-up".

title: M6 — Per-item entries (split multi-food captures)
description:
The fullness / is_beverage / volume features are per-entry, but the capture flow used to
collapse a multi-food photo into one entry — blending four foods into one fullness score
and one volume bucket.

**Granularity = dish/drink, not ingredient.** A burrata salad logs as one item, not
burrata + greens + tomatoes. Only independently-served things separate. Merging an
over-split is trivial (Combine); splitting an under-split is not (no per-piece nutrition
to divide), so the prompt biases toward separating distinct dishes/drinks reliably.

6.1-6.3 shipped. Open: tuning split granularity against real photos (ct-m6.4).

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md "Milestone 6".

title: Tune the model's split granularity against real photos
description:
The only part of M6 the backlog leaves open: whether the prompt reliably separates
distinct dishes/drinks while keeping composite dishes whole. Only verifiable live,
against real photos.

Would be a natural first customer for the eval harness in ct-pm.3.

Source: docs/BACKLOG.md M6 ("Remaining: tuning the model's split granularity").
acceptance_criteria: A representative set of real multi-food photos splits at dish/drink granularity: composite dishes stay whole, independently-served items separate.
